facts.raw_span: 45-year-old man
recent-onset dry cough
exertional dyspnea
no significant past medical history
12 cm mass in the anterior superior mediastinum
multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules suggestive of metastatic disease
neck edema, distended neck veins, and facial plethora
invasion of the superior vena cava above the azygos vein and thrombus extending into the left brachiocephalic trunk
multinodular proliferation of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm
diffuse strong WT1 positivity
moderate, patchy CD99 positivity
rapid symptomatic relief with heparin and high-dose corticosteroids

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a large mediastinal mass, multiple pulmonary nodules, and histopathological findings of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm, along with diffuse strong WT1 positivity and moderate, patchy CD99 positivity, are characteristic of Desmoplastic small round cell tumor.

The patient's symptoms of neck edema, distended neck veins, and facial plethora, along with the radiographic finding of invasion of the superior vena cava, are consistent with Superior vena cava syndrome.
The patient's presentation with thrombus extending into the left brachiocephalic trunk and rapid symptomatic relief with heparin and high-dose corticosteroids suggests Thrombosis.
The patient's presentation with a large mediastinal mass and multiple pulmonary nodules, without a clear histopathological diagnosis, suggests Malignant neoplasm of uncertain histogenesis.

The patient's histopathological findings of a multinodular proliferation of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm, along with diffuse strong WT1 positivity, are consistent with Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor.
The patient's presentation with a large mediastinal mass and multiple pulmonary nodules, without a clear histopathological diagnosis, suggests Lymphoma.
The patient's symptoms of neck edema, distended neck veins, and facial plethora, along with the radiographic finding of invasion of the superior vena cava, are consistent with Vena cava obstruction.
The patient's presentation with a large mediastinal mass and histopathological findings of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm, are consistent with Mediastinal germ cell tumor.
